summary: Iteration 7: tested the new remote:result socket event, remote:command consent (regression), /open and consent_control (regression), and the toasts and hints in the Live Console. Backend: 7 of 7 new tests pass, and all 8 iteration-6 tests pass, including test_targeted_tech_receives_offer_after_open (updated to re-join after /open, as useViewer.js now does). remote:result from the session's own device is relayed to the session room; the technician receives it with from='device'. The error is truncated to exactly 200 characters. It is relayed even while the session is pending. A user socket sending it gets ok:false. A different device sending it gets ok:false and nothing is relayed. remote:command with consent.control=true reaches the device room exactly once. With control=false it returns 'O cliente não autorizou o controlo' and nothing is relayed. Frontend, as admin: in the Consola ao Vivo, a simulated android device (control=true) answered every command with remote:result ok:false 'TEST erro'. Clicking console-nav-back showed a 'TEST erro' toast. A second click 0.5s later still delivered the command, and no second toast appeared (4s throttle works). An android session with control=false shows the 'Ajuda por toque' hint and the nav buttons are disabled. A windows session with control=false shows the 'rato e teclado' hint and the nav buttons are disabled. Native Android/Windows code was not compiled or tested, as instructed.

issues: Long device names are truncated (e.g. 'TEST_it7_sim_an...'), so two devices of the same platform look identical. Consider a tooltip or showing client_name/model.

critical_code_review_comments: remote_result mutates and relays the whole client payload (any extra keys from the device are forwarded). Consider whitelisting {session_id, ok, error, type}.

The remote:result toast falls back to a generic message only when error is empty. Because the backend turns a missing error into '', the fallback works, but ok:true results are silently ignored (fine).
